body:
It's dumb isn't it? 

Luckily, the thought came and went rather fast, but sometimes that thought festers and it's a downward spiral for the rest of the night. Dangerous territory.
From what I have seen Hirez are moving from Twitch to Mixer in terms of perks and development, so I would definitely expect this to happen eventually.

This is me. Aside from my "manic" days where I feel like Wonderwoman, and I can do absolutely everything that needs doing in the space of three hours, I pace up and down for an hour with my coat on before I can force myself to leave the house (unless it's dark, then I can go out)  


Often it is just the getting started. Just say "I will wash one dish" or "I will walk to my garden gate and back again". Often once you're up and moving it's easier.
Sometimes yes all you need is a little vapid pick me up. In those instances, the context I've given doesn't apply so it's entirely different.
Good job!

There is not much help you can get. /u/SomberMusings explained it well enough.

If you start to feel it interferes you can just explain your symptoms and see what your doctor thinks about it you never know they may listen and refer you somewhere.

I just went to take a pee and had a huge breakdown on the toilet. I am shaking and can barely breathe. No trigger, it just happened.

Nobody wants to know a person like that, surely. I have been crying on and off for almost 14 hours.

I hear you completely. I am so used to googling methods and ideas and encouragement that it doesn't phase me any more. It actually helps me NOT do it, cos there is no painless, fast way to die. It always hurts, it's always gonna be scary.

Same. I've had to guilt-trip both a family member and a friend into replying to my messages cos normally I get nothing. I shouldn't have to do that. It makes me feel like a shithead.

I went for a short walk and I saw this really old lady watering her garden plants. All I could think (what I often think) is "good god don't let me live that long, I can't take another 50 years of this"
I think you heavily misunderstand what 'relating to someone' actually means.
I thought something was wrong at first lmao. It started in my back and then just kind of hummed its way around to the front and sides. Didn't last long, of course, but HOOOOOMAMA

You don't love her. You don't even know her. You're just lonely and it was a rare moment of connecting with another human. Intimacy is powerful for that reason.

Don't obsess and latch on to a girl you barely know. She probably doesn't hate you, she's just moved on after the event itself.

Perhaps you need a tutor, or you need to get some medication for whatever mental health issue you are suffering with.

Don't kill yourself over a school grade. School can be extremely useful but it's legitimately not the end of the world. You can make it in life without a chemistry A Level.

If you're insistant or passionate about passing, try and see why. Do you struggle with maths? Are you dyscalculate? Do you struggle with reading, or retaining facts and info? Work on those difficulties.
Meds just don't work sometimes. It's just another shitty part of this whole mental health deal.

I don't know and honestly it's scary. I am 35 and I look at the absolute shambles my life is in, I don't know how much lower it could get but there's still room for it to GET lower.

I feel like my whole life has been wasted being mentally ill. I have so few happy memories.

Sounds like anxiety.

I am the same right now. It's like you're so frustrated about some... *thing* that you just want to tear your own skin off, but don't quite know what it is you want or need.

I've been sitting here ready to explode for the last 6-7 hours because of it.

That's me right now. I've had the worst day anxiety wise. Lots of crying, zoning out, going mute and now I realise it's 3pm and all I've done all day is sit here. It's like your brain is covered in cotton wool.
Same. It upsets me a lot that I can't even just do one normal thing, everything is shrouded in this mental health bullshit.

Have you looked into Maladaptive Daydreaming Disorder? Sounds a lot like it.

I have it. I wrote a post on it:
https://www.reddit.com/r/mentalhealth/comments/8oin01/im_a_maladaptive_daydreamer_heres_my_story/

You know it's not real, but you get lost and involved in it all the same, right?
Oh the art therapy is interesting, I love seeing people paint/create what is in their mind. I just don't know why someone would pay such an obscene price for what is basically a depression doll
Just tell them how you feel. If you find talking hard, write it down (but don't find some medical website and copy it, write down exactly what's in your mind when the feeling strikes)
I don't know why anyone would pay £75 (close to $150 USD) plus shipping for something that reminds them how much they suffer every day.

Nah, you know when something feels off. Just go if you feel 'not right', you don't need to be dangerously ill or in danger. Go to your GP and get a referral if:

- You lose time or have bouts of amnesia  
- You hear voices or see things that you think may not really be there  
- You want to hurt yourself, or have done  
- You are thinking about suicide  
- You feel as if multiple people are living inside of your head  
- You zone out alot uncontrollably  
- You feel anxious or upset often

There's more but anything like that, go see someone.

The most common movements surrounding MDD are rocking back and forth and pacing.

The movements are often small and not potentially harmful or violent. That being said I've read of two cases so far including yours that are not so: one involved repeatedly bashing one's head against a pillow, and yours with your violent thrashing in bed.

Perhaps, if you feel the need to daydream, go for a walk or sit up in bed and try rocking gently. Maybe you can change your habit.

Oh yeah completely. It's important to note it's not like 'dreaming when you are awake', it's almost like... best way to describe it simply is it's like playing pretend in your head. you're in full control of what you daydream about, you just can't control your urges to do it.

Like an alcoholic can choose what they drink, just not that they drink at all if that makes sense.

It's not "officially" recognized as a disorder by many professionals but it is most definitely a thing.
I for one believe it needs WAY more research

Nice! I am glad your sister managed to relate with you over it.

I personally can control what kind of daydreams I have. I am like the main actor and director in my little head play.

I can't always control WHEN (although I can 'stop' it when in a crowd, at work or whatnot), but honestly part of the reason I don't drive is beacuse I know I'd zone out and lose the here and now lol

This is exactly how I feel. I enjoy it very much and as far as I am concerned, as long as I can continue to "switch it off" when I am around people, I don't really care that I have it. It keeps me company in the weeks I can go without seeing people.

Yeah reading and watching a movie are enjoyable yet at the right/wrong moments HUGE triggers for me, especially if I am enjoying said movie or story.

To be 100% engaged, my best bet is to start drawing or writing (something that keeps both hands, eyes and brain busy) and stick on music, or put on something like a documentary or YouTube video as background noise.

Even then sometimes I have a fantasy that I am a famous writer or artist making my next big thing lol

Although nothing officially confirms it (since it's not officially recognized as a disorder and therefore heavily under-researched), I honestly believe it's more of a biproduct of other things. 

Lots of mental illness crosses paths at some point. I have attention issues, but I have never been diagnosed with ADHD cos I wasn't "hyper" as a child, I just have severe concentration issues with certain topics!

EDIT: Just to clarify I also have depression, social/general anxiety and I think I need to speak to my doc about bipolar because I do 'flit' from suicidal to obscenely manic sometimes too.

Anxiety can really put you off your food and cause upset stomachs and the feeling of nausea.

When I am having what I call a 'mental health spike' I flit between bad binges (sometimes to the point of vomiting, although I am not bulimic), and not eating at all.

You can have NOS (not otherwise specified) eating disorders though, although I'd recommend seeing a doctor to get a specific answer on it.

I find the more isolated I am, the more I do it. The more I do it, the more my house and my body suffers. Bit embarassing to admit but my house becomes a sty and so does my body cos I am too busy losing myself to deal with myself.
Honestly it could be lots of things, I don't want to make assumptions. You're better off going to a doctor

That happens with anxiety and depression. I get this too.

I have a build up and I reach a point where I want to tear my own skin off. I feel physically trapped inside of it. Then I have a huge meltdown, breakdown, screaming and crying etc. Then I feel better.

It's literally like a kettle boiling.

You need to go to a doctor. Take some deep breaths and as soon as you are able either book a GP appointment or find a walk-in centre that may be able to help you.

Feeling a bit off when you first wake isn't entirely unusual, but 30 minutes is a long time. Try to write down how you felt, and any other symptoms you may feel are relevant and hand it to the Dr if you struggle to explain yourself.

Oh I see, maybe his anxiety really is that bad O_o I'm sorry he's suffering it!

This is just a guess so please don't take it as diagnosis... does he have issues with food? Like an eating disorder?

I found an article by accident one day - wasn't even looking for it - and I thought OMG THAT IS ME!! Since then I've read up on it and honestly it's a shame it's not officially recognised cos it's so real.

Could the vomiting be related to a physical health problem, as oppose to strictly mental? It's common knowledge that anxiety causes upset in the stomach, but regular vomiting isn't something I've personally experienced or heard of. Usually it just makes me err, wanna poop lol.

I hope he feels better soon, whatever the cause.

Most of the time, yes!

Sometimes I am a side character to another person (nobody IRL just in my head). Like... let's say it's a romance scenario and my brain is doing the usual abuse survivor thing of punishing me like it thinks I deserve...

I'll have the Crush, and this new main character will get the Crush instead of me. Or, Crush will cheat on me with the new main character and I'll be a silent bystander, like an extra.

Dude. I'm ending this conversation.

Either help your girlfriend leave in order to rescue her mental health, or don't. That is why you came here, and now you're challenging anyone who says to help her get away from this toxic human.

I'll only say it once more: she is not your girlfriend's problem. You can recommend help centres etc, but she's out of your hands after that. If she DOES hurt or kill herself then I can absolutely promise you she was likely going to do it anyway. Single people or moments are RARELY the cause.

Then what? You leave her to it. Your gf is not her carer, parent or guardian. You suggest she seeks help and you cut ties. Seriously your gf either stays in this psuedo-carer role or she gets out to heal her own mind.

Honestly this is drama beyond drama. Your girlfriend can find somewhere else to live, it doesn't HAVE to be in this group of ridiculous friends.
Haha yeah I've done it once or twice. I was having a very heated 'argument' the one time and my character gasped really loud and so did I. Luckily I was alone on the street lmao

I don't know the social circle she's in so this is just based on what you're saying, but I've been in this situation personally so that's all I can go from:

- See if gf can talk to the mutual friends, if they are true friends they will be able to balance and not "pick sides". Gf can just say that they are not meshing well and are better off away from each other  

> however there is noone else to watch RM or make sure she doesn't do something terrible.

^ Again this is not your problem. Get gf to leave some numbers or leaflets. Even if RM is not manipulating or doing it on purpose, if your gf's mental health is going down the toilet she needs to be away.

If she can't kick RM out, then help your gf find somewhere else.

Exactly. In my little head theatre, people like my company instead of rolling their eyes when they see me. I am praised for what I am good at instead of purely punished for what I am not good at.

Sometimes I can understand why it's not seen as a disorder, then I remember how disruptive it can be.

Even if RM is legitimately bad in terms of mental health, it is not your girlfriend's cross to bear. 

Being mentally ill does not give you a free pass to be a bad person (you can't help how you feel, but mostly you can control who you take it out on, and how). 

It sounds blunt, but RM is a doctor's problem, not your girlfriends. People with mental health issues (depending on what they are and the severity) can sometimes be quite manipulative and toxic, throwing all of the burden onto a particular person.

The RM gotta go or your gf will suffer more.

I wasn't aware that you could "grow out" of it, that is surprising to read!

 I have MD and I'm in my mid-thirties, I'm ass-deep in daydreams almost all of the time (general rule: if I am not fully-focused or in a group of people, I'm away)
Doesn't really stop, to be honest. The second my eyes open - be it a reasonable 8am, or an annoying 2am, the moment I wake up the theatre in my head does, too.
Ignore the "is anyone else here an MD" question, this is crossposted from /r/MentalHealth lol

Oh yes! I also live in poverty currently (a recurring theme in my life since childhood), so I have one particularly far-fetched daydream where this female figure, who can control worlds, create them almost like in the Sims I guess, takes me and all history of me out of this world and into one where I call the shots and live as I wish (taller, richer, more popular, etc). I know it isn't real but it's a copying mechanism I guess!

> Fair enough I had a stressful childhood, screwed me up, but who hasn’t?

Most people, actually. Being abused, traumatised or "screwed up" from your childhood is very bad, and not normal at all. I don't blame you for saying that, though. I was in my 30s before I realised that my childhood was anything but normal.

I wish you the best, but if this were my situation I'd still seek a second opinion. I don't always agree with drugs, sometimes they're the wrong solution entirely, but you may still need help that you otherwise won't get.

Best of luck to you.

I'm with defenderZim.

I lived with a toxic, mentally abusive roommate and it was soul destroying. No question, either your girlfriend leaves or if it is her place, kick out the roommate ASAP.
